column1: # 🟢 EMEA / SPAIN — NEW, and found ONLY in Spanish. Spain's Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación
# y Universidades is preparing a Real Decreto de enseñanzas universitarias which will, FOR THE
# FIRST TIME, carry an article specific to AI in university teaching. It is negotiated with
# CRUE and student representatives and frames AI across FOUR planes — the classroom,
# institutional use, research, and the university's own administration. The Secretary General
# of Universities, Francisco García Pascual, states an ETHICAL CODE for AI use will be
# OBLIGATORY. Intended publication in the BOE before the academic year ends.
# 🔴 Dated to APRIL 2026 at source, so whether it has since been published is NOT established
# here and is NOT asserted. ATTRIBUTED-UNVERIFIED: the BOE itself was not read — no non-GitHub
# citation address was reachable by either tool this pass (see the channel probe).
# 🟡 EMEA / GERMANY — A QUALIFICATION OF p381'S OWN HEADLINE, which is why this leg was re-run.
# p381 published `openDesk Edu` in "8 600 SCHOOLS" as "THE LARGEST NAMED OPEN-SOURCE EDUCATION
# DEPLOYMENT THIS BASE HAS EVER RECORDED". The German leg re-run here returns the same single
# origin — a borncity news item — and the leg's own summary states that the article rests on
# that ONE source and that no official confirmation was found.
# 🔴 So the 8 600 figure is SINGLE-SOURCED SECONDARY REPORTING, not an official deployment
# record, and p381's superlative rests on it. It is NOT withdrawn — a single source is still a
# source — but it is DOWNGRADED to ATTRIBUTED-UNVERIFIED and the superlative is retired until
# an official ZenDiS or ministry record is read first-hand.
# 🟢 What IS newly established and consistent: the integration is dated 29 July 2026, it unites
# the LMS `ILIAS` with `OpenProject` behind single sign-on, the suite is built by ZenDiS
# (Centre for Digital Sovereignty in Public Administration), and it was first used at the
# Ministerpräsidentenkonferenz in October 2024.
# 🟢 A SECOND German instrument, new: the Ergebnisbericht of the conference "Offene KI in der
# Schule 2026", which recommends using the Digitalpakt 2.0 window to build sovereign,
# data-protection-compliant, scalable AI infrastructure for schools, and notes that open-source
# strategies already exist in many Bundesländer.
# 🟢 LATAM — method-bearing for a third consecutive pass, and p382 adds a BREAKDOWN p381 lacked.
# UNESCO IESALC / UNU-IAS, 200 institutions across 19 countries, fielded Aug–Oct 2025:
#     teaching and learning  73.5 %   |   research        57.0 %
#     administration         34.1 %   |   community       20.0 %
#   🔵 p381 carried the 200/19 sample but not the per-function split. The ORDER is the finding:
#      adoption is deepest exactly where governance is thinnest.
# Digital Education Council + Tecnológico de Monterrey (Institute for the Future of Education),
# 29 LATAM institutions, >30 000 responses, released February 2026: 92 % of students and
#     🟢 79 % OF FACULTY actively engaging with AI. p381 had the student figure; the faculty
#     figure is new here, and it is the one that matters to a studio — faculty are the buyers.
# Regulation: Chile has had a National AI Policy since 2021 with a law under discussion; Brazil
#     and Colombia have national strategies but NO education-specific rules; Mexico's SEP,
#     ANUIES and Observatorio IA guidance is explicitly NON-BINDING. ~30 % of LATAM universities
#     have published an AI-use policy (Tec de Monterrey, Bossio).
# Players: Digital Education Council · Tec de Monterrey IFE · UNESCO IESALC · UNU-IAS · UNAM ·
#     UPC (Peru) · IDB and CEPAL (the ILIA index, 19 countries) · SEP and ANUIES (Mexico).
# 🔴 THE NORTH AMERICA REGRESSION, AND IT IS A FINDING ABOUT THIS BASE'S OWN METHOD.
# p381 REFUSED nine figures by name. Its list included: `$951 M -> $2.3 B`, the `36 %` NA share,
# `10 %` formal-guidelines, `71 %` untrained teachers, and the `92 % -> 66 %` student-usage
# splice. p382's North America leg returned `$951 M -> $2.3 B` (15.9 % CAGR), `36 %` NA share,
# `10 %` with formal AI guidelines and `71 %` of US teachers lacking AI training — THE SAME SET,
# from the same class of source, one pass later.
# 🔵 A REFUSED FIGURE IS NOT A RETIRED FIGURE. Refusal is a decision about what this base
# publishes; it does nothing to the channel, which re-serves the figure on the next sweep. So a
# refusal must be WRITTEN DOWN AS A REFUSAL and re-matched on arrival, or every pass pays the
# adjudication cost again. `ACTION SH`'s refuted-claims table is exactly this instrument, and
# the regression here is the argument for running it on INTAKE rather than at write-up.
# 🟢 AND THE SPLICE MECHANISM, NAMED AT LAST. p381 refused "92 % -> 66 % student usage" as a
# cross-population splice but could not say where the halves came from. p382 can: the 92 % is
# the DIGITAL EDUCATION COUNCIL'S **LATAM** FIGURE (29 LATAM institutions, Feb 2026), and the
# 66 % is a 2024 GLOBAL figure. The splice takes a LATAM survey result and presents it as a
# global year-on-year rise. 🔵 Both halves are real; the sentence joining them is not.
